accroche: Oil can date from the age of the dinosaurs without coming from them: its material comes mostly from marine algae and plankton, buried and then heated.
contenu_vulgarise:
You often hear that oil is made of dinosaurs, buried and compressed for millions of years. The idea is persistent, and wrong.

## What the green dinosaur says

Since 1930, a green dinosaur has served as the emblem of the American brand Sinclair. According to the company's own history, its copywriters introduced it to promote lubricants made from Pennsylvania crude oils, presented as having been deposited in the Mesozoic, when dinosaurs roamed the Earth. The Apatosaurus is registered as a trademark in 1932, and the firm's exhibit in Chicago in 1933-1934 draws more than 24,000 visitors a day. The company history does not say the oil is made of dinosaurs: it ties it to an era. And that era is doubtful: the oil-bearing sandstones of Venango, in the county where Edwin Drake drilled what is considered the world's first commercial well, are Late Devonian according to the U.S. Geological Survey, well before the Mesozoic. For these reservoirs at least, the advertising's dating is wrong. And even if it were right, an era is not a raw material.

## The raw material

The geologist Reidar Müller of the University of Oslo describes a different chain of events. Microscopic algae and plankton die and fall to the seafloor. Their remains pile up in thick layers, covered by clay and sand. Buried a few kilometers down, at around 60 to 120 °C, they are cooked by heat and pressure and become oil, which rises through porous rock until a dense layer stops it. The sea of that time, about 150 million years ago in his example, was short of oxygen: little life on the bottom, so few scavengers, and remains that pile up instead of being eaten.

## How we know

The trail is chemical. In 1936, Alfred Treibs publishes a paper whose title refers to chlorophyll and hemin derivatives in organic mineral substances. According to the geochemist Keith Kvenvolden, Treibs described porphyrin-type pigments in shales, coals, and crude oils, and traced their origin back to biological precursors. Kvenvolden sees him as the father of organic geochemistry.

## What the story shifts

Müller adds a caveat. A dinosaur bone has been found in a Norwegian well, and marine reptiles, plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs, lie in the same Svalbard layer as oil. Some oil might come from such reptiles, he thinks, but they are not dinosaurs, and the idea of oil made of dinosaurs remains pure fantasy to him. Most of the material is something else, and more modest: cells that no one can see with the naked eye.

Dating a rock to the age of the dinosaurs says when it formed, not what it is made of. How many other received ideas confuse the era of an object with what it is made of?

repere.texte: According to the geologist Reidar Müller (University of Oslo), oil comes from trillions of microscopic algae and plankton, buried a few kilometers down and heated to around 60 to 120 °C. He considers the idea of an origin in dinosaurs pure fantasy.
repere.source: Ingrid Schou, “No, oil does not come from dinosaurs,” Sciencenorway.no, May 14, 2022

carte.punch: Oil from the age of the dinosaurs: made mostly of algae and plankton, not dinosaurs.
carte.idee: Oil comes mostly from marine algae and plankton that pile up on the floor of an oxygen-poor sea (150 million years ago in Müller's example), are buried, and are then cooked at around 60 to 120 °C. According to Kvenvolden, Treibs links pigments in oil to biological precursors in 1936.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Treibs, “Chlorophyll- und Häminderivate in organischen Mineralstoffen”, Angewandte Chemie, 49, 682-686 (1936)
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The 1936 paper on porphyrins in oils, shales, and coals.

quiz.question: According to the geologist Reidar Müller, what is oil mostly made of, and why did that material accumulate?
choix: Large land reptiles buried in swamps, sheltered from oxygen and scavengers
Whole forests buried and turned into oil by the pressure of sediments alone
Marine algae and plankton, preserved on the floor of an oxygen-poor sea
Dead fish and shellfish, turned into oil by fermentation near the surface
quiz.explication: Müller describes algae and plankton that sink, pile up, and are buried; the lack of oxygen limited life on the bottom, so the remains were not eaten. Neither dinosaurs nor forests: to him, the idea of an origin in dinosaurs is pure fantasy. The reptiles Müller mentions are marine, and for Müller the oil is cooked by heat after burial, not fermented near the surface.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the green Apatosaurus of the Sinclair brand, in use since 1930, represent?
choix: An advertising emblem for lubricants made from Pennsylvania oils
Scientific proof that oil is made of dinosaurs
The name of an oil field discovered by the Sinclair company
A symbol adopted after fossils were found in one of the company's wells
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says this dinosaur has served as an emblem since 1930 to promote lubricants made from Pennsylvania crude oils, and that the company history does not claim the oil is made of dinosaurs.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the U.S. Geological Survey, what is the age of the oil-bearing sandstones of Venango, Pennsylvania?
choix: Mesozoic, as the Sinclair advertising claims
Jurassic, the age of the great dinosaurs
Late Devonian, well before the Mesozoic
Cretaceous, just before the dinosaurs disappeared
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text cites the USGS: these sandstones are Late Devonian, well before the Mesozoic, where the Sinclair advertising wrongly places these oils.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What exception does Müller cite, in which a little oil might come from an animal other than algae or plankton?
choix: Herds of herbivorous dinosaurs fossilized in tropical swamps
Marine reptiles found in the same Svalbard layer as oil
Fossilized corals that trapped oil in their ancient skeletons
Entire tropical forests swallowed by a very sudden flood
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says a little oil might come from marine reptiles, plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs, found with oil in Svalbard, but that these are not dinosaurs.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In 1936, what does Alfred Treibs publish, according to the card?
choix: An official report on the precise dating of the Pennsylvania sandstones
A detailed study of the temperature at which oil is cooked
A paper showing that oil contains dinosaur DNA
A paper on chlorophyll derivatives in organic materials
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says Treibs publishes in 1936 a paper on chlorophyll and hemin derivatives in organic mineral substances, which makes him, for Kvenvolden, the father of organic geochemistry.
